items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: And they had, what, here's a guy with a sub-tone, Chester Hazlett and they had so many things that you could use and good musical surroundings

ctx.x: looked very solid and besides there was a guy, Ferdie Grofé, who -- I had never met him, but I was always a great admirer of his music ability, his arranging, and then there was Jimmy. He said, "You ought to come with us," and Tommy was in the band then and Red Nichols had left, had been in the band and left and there was some talk of Miff, but I understand that Miff never got to the band. At that time.

And they had, what, here's a guy with a sub-tone, Chester Hazlett and they had so many things that you could use and good musical surroundings, Malneck, and they had a saxophone player, Max Farley and then they had the Rhythm Boys, which didn't particularly appeal to me. You know, I didn't know them -- they also had another trio that they used to use quite a bit. They had six singers, so as far as I was concerned, I was looking forward to September and the end of the job.

So I stayed with the band until the end of that engagement. Then another weekend, down comes Rollini, Adrian, and he said that he wanted to know the same thing, "What are you guys going to do?" And he wants to take all the guys but he won't have Steve Brown. Steve Brown was a big feature in our band, because he plays bass himself, but the bass fiddle is out.
